title: Ode to Joy
short: Ludwig van Beethoven · C 4/4 · play it with every note lit.

blocks.html: Beethoven’s tune moves almost entirely by step, so it’s a good first tune for low-G tuning. Most of it sits on the 2nd and 3rd strings; in bar 12 the tune drops to the low G, the open 4th string, a note a high-G ukulele doesn’t have. Pick it with your thumb or index finger, then strum C and G7 with down-up eighths, or play the tune while a friend strums.

blocks.name: music-player
blocks.cap: Play it: the score scrolls, the keys or strings light up as each note sounds.

blocks.html: The piece: Symphony No. 9 in D minor, Op. 125 (1824), last movement: the main theme

sources.name: Melody as in our piano version of Ode to Joy, which was checked note by note against the Mutopia Project’s “Ode to Joy” hymn setting (public domain). The chords are our own. Our checking script compares the two melodies beat by beat.
